title: SRE Evidence-to-Action Handbook: From Incident Forensics to Capacity & SLO Remediation
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
This handbook defines a prescriptive, auditable pipeline for converting incident evidence and post-incident findings into concrete SLO, error-budget, capacity, and tooling actions. The goal is to shorten the time from "discovery -> evidence -> decision -> remediation" while preserving blamelessness and traceability.

Audience
- SRE oncall and rotation leads
- Service owners and service reliability stewards
- Product managers responsible for tiered SLAs
- Capacity and forecasting teams

Why this exists
- We frequently collect high-quality forensic evidence in incident reviews but lack a standardized path that guarantees remediation (capacity, SLOs, tooling changes) is implemented and validated.
- This doc codifies who decides, how we prioritize, how we measure remediation success, and how evidence is stored and linked.

Key principles
- Evidence-first: every action must be linked to evidence items (logs, replays, synthetic canaries, graphs, sample tokens).
- Minimal viable remediation: prefer fast, reversible mitigations (traffic shaping, temporary headroom) while planning permanent fixes.
- Ownership and deadlines: each remediation item has an owner, ETA, verification steps, and a quality gate.
- Playbookable: run the same steps for incidents of similar class (latency spike, OOM cascade, model regression, capacity saturation).

High-level pipeline (4 stages)
1) Capture (During incident)
   - Assign an evidence recorder (oncall SRE) to collect: dashboards snapshot, p50/p95/p99 latency slices, error counts by tenant, representative request/response pairs, kernel/oom logs, Kubernetes pod events, heap/gc traces, KV cache usage, model cache hit/miss rates.
   - Use the incident evidence collector script: 
     curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVID_TOKEN" https://telemetry.internal/api/incident/capture?incident=$INCIDENT_ID > evidence_bundle.json
2) Triage (Post-incident 0-72 hours)
   - Run an evidence triage meeting within 72 hours; attendees: incident commander, service owner, one SRE steward, one oncall from runtime.
   - Classify root cause types: capacity headroom, model regression, infra degradation, config rollback, downstream outage, traffic spike, buggy client.
   - Produce an Evidence Summary doc (link to evidence_bundle) with minimal reproducible steps.
3) Remediate (7-30 days)
   - For each remediation candidate create a Remediation Item in the SRE action tracker. Each item must include: title, owner, priority (P0/P1/P2), blocking_flags, acceptance_criteria, expected cost/impact, rollback plan, and verification steps.
   - Example remediation types: capacity resize, autoscale tuning, token-priority throttle, model rollback/patch, patch to runtime kernel, cache warm pool augmentation, new synthetic canary.
4) Verify & Close (post-remediation)
   - Run the verification checklist in a production shadowed environment or using mirrored traffic. Verification must include: synthetic canary pass (7d), P95 latency return within X% of baseline, error rate below SLO by at least 95th percentile, unit-cost impact under budget.
   - Close the remediation item only after verification and update the incident review with links to the action and evidence.

Decision authority and cadence
- Day 0 triage decisions (fast mitigations): incident commander + SRE oncall may approve rolling back a model, enabling burst capacity, or applying a temporary traffic throttle. These require automated audit entries.
- Permanent capacity changes and SLO adjustments: require service steward approval + capacity planning representative + product manager sign-off for contractual SLOs.
- Emergency overprovisioning (>= 12 hours queue build): SRE Director must be notified and approval logged.

Remediation priority matrix
- P0: Customer-facing outage or sustained SLO breach > 4 hours, action must start within 4 hours.
- P1: Intermittent SLO breach or elevated burn rate, action must be planned within 72 hours and executed within 14 days.
- P2: Quality regressions or non-critical platform improvements, plan in next sprint.

SLO & Error-budget action guidelines (quick reference)
- If error-budget burn rate > 5x for 1 hour OR > 2x for 6 hours: open a P1 remediation item, enable conservative throttling for non-critical tenants, notify product.
- If sustained SLO breach (p95 latency > target for 3 consecutive measurement intervals): create rollback/fallback plan and schedule a canary of candidate fixes.
- For model-serving-specific SLOs: track token-rate headroom (tokens/sec capacity) and KV cache efficacy; if token-headroom < 20% for 1 hour, apply tenant priority gating.

Capacity planning integration
- Post-incident capacity action must be translated into an updated capacity forecast within the Capacity Ledger.
- Capacity change workflow: 
  1. Submit a Capacity Change Request (CCR) with inputs: observed peak qps, sustained 95th seq_len distribution, quantization mode, expected growth, business justification.
  2. Capacity team responds with: estimated hardware (GPU count/instance type), cost delta, lead time.
  3. Schedule deployment during off-peak (if possible) and create verification load test.
- Sizing heuristics (example):
  - Token throughput per A100-80GB (baseline serving runtime): ~1.2M tokens/sec for short sequences (<=64) under continuous batching; adjust by sequence-length multiplier = 0.8 + 0.02 * (avg_seq_len - 64)
  - Add safety headroom = max(20% of baseline, 2 * 99th token burst estimate)

Template: Capacity Change Request (CCR)
| field | example | notes |
|---|---|---|
| service | embed-service-prod | service id in catalog |
| observed_peak_tokens/sec | 320000 | 15-min sliding window |
| avg_seq_len | 128 | token estimate for requests |
| current_capacity | 3 x A100-80GB | units in inventory |
| requested_change | +2 A100-80GB | scaled up to absorb peak |
| justification | sustained p95 latency breach during sale event | attach incident link |
| requested_by | service-steward@example.com | |

Operational tooling: automated evidence and remediation SDKs
- Evidence Collector CLI (evidencectl)
  - capture: evidencectl capture --incident $ID --out incident-123.json\  - upload: evidencectl upload --file incident-123.json --project $SERVICE
- Remediation item creation via API:
  curl -X POST https://sre-actions.internal/api/items \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"title":"Increase model warm-pool","owner":"@oncall-alex","priority":"P1","related_incident":"INC-2025-456","acceptance_criteria":"p95 latency within 10% of baseline for 7d"}'

Runbook fragments (playable steps)
- Latency spike (p95) due to quantized-serving regression
  1. Evidence: collect p95 timeline, quantization flag distribution, node-level GPU utilization.
  2. Fast mitigation: disable quantized path for affected model (feature-flag) and roll forward to verified variant.
  3. Medium-term remediation: add canary pipeline for quantized kernels + add quantization-specific latency synthetic.
  4. Verification: synthetic canary run for 72 hours at production-like qps.

- Token headroom exhaustion (sustained)
  1. Evidence: per-tenant token consumption, token-priority queue lengths, model warm-pool utilization.
  2. Fast mitigation: apply token-priority gating for lower-tier tenants (using traffic-shepherd service).
  3. Capacity request: open CCR and schedule scale-up.
  4. Post-scaling verification: validate 7-day synthetic and spot-check customer flows.

Incident review standards (evidence and artifacts checklist)
- Required for all P0/P1 incidents:
  - Full packet: timeline, raw logs (redacted), grafana snapshots, heap/dump (if applicable), replay steps, representative request samples (masked PII), list of commands executed by responders.
  - Evidence retention: store immutable evidence bundle in SRE evidence bucket for 1 year (default) and link in incident doc.
  - Forensics owner: named SRE responsible for evidence integrity and replayability.

Acceptance criteria for remediation closure
- All remediation items must meet these gates before closure:
  1. Evidence link(s) attached and reproducibility steps documented.
  2. Synthetic or shadow verification executed and passing for configured window (default 7 days).
  3. If change affected billing/cost, finance-notify run and cost delta documented.
  4. Post-change SLO telemetry reviewed and thumbed by service steward.

Tracking & dashboards
- Required dashboards for every service (templated):
  - SLO dashboard: p50/p95/p99, error rate, burn rate, error-budget remaining (7d/30d).
  - Capacity dashboard: tokens/sec headroom, warm pool hit-rate, GPU utilization by cluster, pending scale requests.
  - Evidence catalog view: list of open remediation items linked to incidents and evidence bundles.

Change control and audit requirements
- Any fast mitigation performed by oncall must create an automated audit entry within 1 hour: who, what, why, linked evidence, revert plan.
- Permanent changes that affect SLOs or contractual obligations need change approval ticket and communication to affected customers.

Playbook for post-incident retrospective (2-week timeline)
1. Day 0-3: evidence capture + triage + create remediation items.
2. Day 4-10: implement short-term mitigations and schedule CCRs where necessary.
3. Day 11-14: verification runs and finalize action owners.
4. 2-week retro session to capture lessons and update runbooks.

Appendix A: Common CLI snippets and examples
- Collect a 15-minute Grafana snapshot and upload:
  grafana-snapshot --dashboard svc-slo --from -15m --to now --out svc-slo-15m.png && evidencectl upload --file svc-slo-15m.png --meta incident=INC-2025-456
- Sample token headroom query (PromQL):
  sum by(cluster) (rate(tokens_consumed_total[5m]))
- Example acceptance JSON for remediation API:
  {
    "title": "Add 2x A100 to embed-service-prod",
    "owner": "oncall-alex",
    "priority": "P1",
    "acceptance_criteria": "p95 latency <= baseline * 1.10 for 7d"
  }

Appendix B: Roles & Responsibilities (short)
- Incident Commander: owns evidence capture and highest-priority fast mitigations.
- Service Steward: owns long-term remediation and SLO contracts.
- Capacity Planner: translates CCR to procurement/resize.
- SRE Forensics Owner: ensures evidence bundles are reproducible and retained.

Feedback & improvements
- This handbook is reviewed quarterly by the SRE steering committee. To propose changes, open a PR against this page and tag the reviewers listed above.

Related policies and templates
- See: Incident Evidence Handoff Procedure, Capacity Onboarding Playbook, SLO Admission Checklist.
